claims.text: The starting material is equimolar CoCrFeNiTi, corresponding to approximately 20 at.% of each element.
The starting CoCrFeNiTi is in an as-cast or solution-treated simple solid-solution state.
Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in the simple solid-solution state has relatively low hardness and strength combined with high ductility.
The combination of low hardness and strength with high ductility is governed by the absence of precipitation strengthening.
No fine precipitates or ordered domains impede dislocation glide in the simple solid-solution state.
Dislocations consequently experience low resistance to motion in the simple solid-solution state.
A controlled aging treatment at 600 °C can induce nanoscale intermetallic or ordered precipitates in equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
The aging duration affects whether precipitation occurs and the resulting precipitate size and distribution.
Nanoscale ordered precipitates act as obstacles to dislocation movement.
The aging-induced precipitates strengthen CoCrFeNiTi by pinning or impeding dislocations.
Aged CoCrFeNiTi will have greater hardness than the unaged simple-solid-solution control.
Aged CoCrFeNiTi will have greater compressive strength than the unaged simple-solid-solution control.
Aged CoCrFeNiTi will exhibit lower compressive plastic strain than the unaged control.
The proposed comparison holds composition constant and compares an unaged simple-solid-solution control with a sample aged at 600 °C.
The hypothesis is limited to hardness and compressive-loading evaluations at test temperatures up to 600 °C.
The magnitude of strengthening depends on aging duration and precipitate size and distribution.
